speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: asked the Minister for Education (a) whether the Ministry tracks the take-up rate of school-based and community-based Student Care Centres (SCC); (b) if so, what are the take-up rates respectively; and (c) whether programmes under these SCCs can be further enhanced to include additional enrichment activities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Education)
text: MOE regularly engages school-based SCCs on their programmes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Education)
text: These SCCs have the flexibility to offer programmes and additional enrichment activities to meet the needs of their students.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: It has been quite a number of years since we introduced the SCCs.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: I believe they still serve a good purpose, especially for latch-key kids whose parents are working.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Now that this has been implemented for a number of years, can I ask the Minister of State if MOE would do a fresh review, to see if the programmes can be updated further or can be enhanced, especially, given the emphasis now to embrace learning beyond grades, so, whether the SCCs can be aligned to that as well?

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: MOE recognises the importance of holistic development of our students and, as mentioned, our school-based SCCs provide outdoor programmes, enrichment activities to develop values and 21st century competencies in our students.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: And this is in line with our direction to go beyond grades.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: Schools also work with SCCs and community partners to support Learning and Development of our students in different ways.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: For example, the National Library Board conducts reading programmes to cultivate the love for reading in our students.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: RSVP Singapore organises interest-based activities to engage our SCC students, so that they are imparted with life skills and values.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: The Minister of State mentioned 33,000 for school-based SCCs and 8,000 for the community-based SCCs.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: So, whether we have seen more or higher demand and whether there will be more SCCs to be provided, if so.
